content.text: {"relation": "DIVERGENT", "consensus_summary": "Blind consensus: butter/curds primarily symbolizes abundance, prosperity, and God's rich provision from the land (Deut 32:14; Job 20:17; Job 29:6; Isa 7:22), with common alternatives of subsistence food amid devastation (Isa 7:15, 21-22), hospitality (Gen 18:8; Judg 5:25), flattering deceitful speech (Ps 55:21), the product of pressure/churning (Prov 30:33), and minority/rare patristic-allegorical readings of Christ's incarnation or doctrinal richness. No settled single consensus.", "book_summary": "The book identifies butter as the word worked (churned) from milk into sound judgment — teaching tested and matured until one can refuse evil and choose good (Isa 7:15 via Prov 30:33's churning image). Applied to the walk it cleanses the feet (Job 29:6 linked to John 13:5-10), and its counterfeit is smooth speech concealing war (Ps 55:21).", "consensus_core_identification": "Butter/curds = abundance, richness, and divine material provision (the fatness of the land).", "book_core_identification": "Butter = the word/teaching processed from milk into mature discernment (sound judgment enabling one to refuse evil and choose good), which cleanses the believer's walk.", "core_relation": "CONTRADICTS", "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION", "boundary_disagreement": "The book keeps several consensus proof-texts but reassigns their sense: Job 29:6 moves from a poetic emblem of former prosperity to feet-cleansing by the word (paired with John 13); Isaiah 7:15 moves from the abundance-vs-subsistence/incarnation debate to a definition of butter as discernment-producing teaching; Proverbs 30:33 moves from an analogy about provocation and strife to the positive mechanism by which the word is 'worked' into butter. Psalm 55:21 is retained but reframed as the symbol's counterfeit rather than an independent figurative use. The dominant consensus extension — abundance/prosperity passages read as material blessing — is effectively dropped as the core.", "material_contradiction": "The consensus's central identification (material abundance and prosperity of the land) is replaced by a spiritual-epistemic identification (matured word producing sound judgment and cleansing the walk). One cannot hold that butter's core symbolic referent is material plenty while also holding it is processed doctrine yielding discernment; the book does not present its reading as one sense among many but as the identification, reclassifying the very verses the consensus uses for abundance.", "rationale": "The book's core is not covered by the consensus primary meaning and only partially anticipated by a rare/minority alternative (patristic 'doctrinal richness/mature revelation' readings in Responses A and C), so it is not NOVEL; but because it displaces the abundance core rather than adjusting its boundary, it is DIVERGENT rather than REFINED. The book builds a systematic derivation — milk (elementary word) churned by pressure into butter (mature judgment, Prov 30:33 + Isa 7:15), which then cleanses the walk (Job 29:6 + John 13) — a construction absent from every consensus primary and only loosely gestured at in the rare alternatives. The extension shows partial reclassification: shared verses are retained under new senses, and the flattery use is subordinated as counterfeit.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "Responses A and C both list allegorical readings of butter as the richness of divine doctrine or 'mature revelation' as minority/rare alternatives, and Isaiah 7:15 explicitly ties eating butter to knowing to refuse evil and choose good; one could argue the book merely elevates and refines an acknowledged alternative (REFINED) rather than contradicting the tradition, especially since the consensus itself reports no settled meaning. However, the book's wholesale reclassification of the abundance proof-texts (Job 29:6, 2 Sam 17:29) and its dependence on an unstated milk-as-word premise plus a butter/water conflation in John 13 (which mentions no butter) mark this as replacement of the central referent rather than boundary adjustment.", "confidence": "medium"}
